particularites.text: High FX exposure (~50% of revenue outside the euro area, notably USD), with no complete natural hedge described: a structural cause of volatility in reported income from one year to the next.

Unique proprietary sales model: more than 630 former chefs employed as a direct sales force (335 000 customer visits in 2025), creating a "pull" effect that competitors (10x larger) can hardly replicate and securing organic growth independently of dealer networks.

ownership.insiderDesc: Family control block stemming from founder Siegfried Meister (died in 2017, held 63,7%): Franziska Würbser (15,99%, having received her mother Gabriella Meister's stake in 2025), Gabriella Meister (15,76%), Ulrike Meister (15,59%), and Walter Kurtz (7,81%, co-founder 1973, still on the Supervisory Board with his son Moritz Graser). Franziska Würbser and Walter Kurtz/Siegfried Meister have a statutory joint right to appoint up to two Supervisory Board members for as long as they are shareholders.

compliance.note: No established fraud and no allegation by a regulator, a plaintiffs' law firm or an activist short seller identified to date (search of 07/08/2026) - company not listed in the United States, outside the post-share-price-decline solicitation regime that is frequent on US stocks.

clesRetenues: Q Investor (need to continue ramping up the sales force) - the CEO confirms an ongoing process, necessary to feed growth, with a direct causality already shown between adding salespeople and sales development (tightening sales territories).
Q Investor (China, iCombi One acceptance and return to growth) - the CEO says the company does not publish detailed figures on the iCombi One but is satisfied with progress at this stage.

Q Investor (iHexagon update) - the CEO confirms that no precise figures are published, says he is satisfied with the development, and reports a growing number of customers who see a real benefit from it.

Q Investor (region driving the iVario in H1 and the H2 outlook) - the CFO indicates that the United States, France and Iberia (Spain/Portugal) carried most of the growth, and says he is confident of maintaining an iVario growth rate twice that of the iCombi.

Q Investor (Chinese market, iCombi One acceptance, key account contracts) - the CEO reports Chinese consumer sentiment still depressed, the main headwind being Yum China's (KFC) shift away towards local sourcing; the dedicated iCombi One sales team is in place, new dealers are being won every month, and a contract with a new key account has already been secured.

Q Investor (US competitors increasing local production in the face of tariffs, is RATIONAL considering investing in the US) - the CEO replies that he does not observe this phenomenon among competitors and that the overall situation for US production is assessed regularly, with no concrete plan at this stage.

Q Investor (rise in the order book at end-Q2, July trends) - the CFO attributes the rise in the order book (10-15 M€ vs previous quarters) to a strong order flow in June (United States, Germany, Canada in the lead) not fully delivered before quarter-end, and expects that order book to support a positive development in H2.

Q Investor (South Asia, gap vs last year) - the CFO attributes the gap mainly to Australia and to a timing effect linked to the restocking of a large partner, with no structural change over a longer period.

Q Investor (reasons for the strong growth in the DACH region) - the CFO explains German growth by one-off stock orders from several dealers in Q1 (Q2 growth broad-based and with no notable one-off effect), Austrian growth by the recapture of an Aldi tender, and Switzerland by solid commercial execution with no specific one-off factor.

Q Investor (impact of the Middle East conflict) - the CEO confirms a limited impact: the region accounts for ~2-3% of group revenue, a decline of around 2 M€ recorded in H1, higher costs but no material supply disruption anticipated.

Q Investor (drivers of the >10% North American growth at constant currency in H1) - the CEO reaffirms North America as the group's number 1 growth market given the still very open potential, with organic growth >10% the expected pace.

Q Investor (volume/price split of Q2 growth of ~4%) - the CEO indicates that the majority of H1 growth (+6% reported) comes from underlying volume, a smaller share from regional mix, and a minor impact from price increases; in Q2 specifically, volume remains the main driver, with price increases starting to contribute modestly.
Q Investor (cost of customs tariffs expected in H2) - the CFO puts the full-year tariff impact at ~28-29 M€, with an H2 effect slightly below H1 thanks to the decline in tariff rates.

Q Investor (trajectory of procurement costs excluding the tariff refund, ~9% increase in H1) - the CFO confirms a comparable rate of increase expected in H2, driven by steel, chemicals and above all the electronics sector, with no easing expected in the near term.

Q Investor (additional energy costs vs 2025) - the CFO puts the direct effect at a very limited level (~3 M€ gas/electricity, ~2,5 M€ fleet fuel, annual net effect ~0,5 M€), with most of the energy pressure passing through to customers and suppliers rather than to RATIONAL directly.
Q Investor (trajectory of wage costs) - the CFO confirms the annual July pay increase at ~3,8% on average in Germany, aligned with inflation and the metalworking sector negotiations.

Q Investor (the tariff refund will not recur in 2027, possibility of price increases to offset higher costs) - the CEO confirms several scenarios under review, with the historical preference going to operational efficiency rather than price increases, but a modest price increase remains contemplated if the scale of the costs exceeds what efficiency can absorb.

Q Investor (validity of the 10% tariff -> 6-7% price increase calculation to preserve the absolute contribution) - the CFO confirms that the mathematical ratio remains valid, but that the baseline assumption of a 10% tariff no longer applies: for 2027, the expected average rate is more like ~14%.

Q Investor (return on the spare parts investment at Landsberg, revenue mix, CapEx 2027) - the CFO specifies that the decision to extend the spare parts building targets growth and service availability, not cost reduction (no scale effect expected, rather ramp-up costs, ~1,5-2 M€ of additional depreciation once fully operational); completion planned for early 2027, with in parallel the start of construction of a new customer experience centre at Landsberg in mid-2027.

Q Investor (update on H2 guidance, input costs, demand trends, key markets Germany/North America) - the CFO reports mixed input costs (base steel stable, alloy surcharges higher than expected, freight high but stabilised), demand supported by a healthy order book, a Germany whose momentum should continue without any certainty of repeating the exceptional pace of H1, and a North America kept within the 10-15% growth range expected for the year.

Q Investor (sharp rise in inventories, ~10%) - the CFO attributes the rise to the opening of a new warehouse in Dubai and to a seasonal build-up of inventories in overseas markets to secure delivery times.

Q Investor (trajectory of accounts payable) - the CFO indicates that this line remains limited in size and broadly stable, with the quarterly variations being timing effects and no specific issue identified on their side.

Q Investor (high equity ratio, ~80%, openness to buybacks given the share price level) - the CFO rules out the buyback option (free float already low, not to be reduced further), reaffirms the unwritten distribution policy of a ~70% payout plus a special dividend if liquidity allows, and mentions the possibility of a further special dividend in the future if the cash position justifies it.

Q Investor (2027 tariff impact expected at ~28-29 M€ as in 2026) - the CFO confirms a similar order of magnitude, potentially 2-3 M€ higher owing to the growth in business volume in the United States.

Q Investor (competitive intensity in China, local competitors, can the iCombi One win back market share) - the CEO identifies two main local competitors (Justa and a second player), positioned on lower quality/service and lower prices; the iCombi One aims to be price-competitive against them while retaining superior cooking quality, with list-price positioning slightly above.

hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
Uncontested world leader in professional combi-ovens. H1 2026 confirms the thesis integrally: revenue +8% organic (641.5M), EBIT +11% (169.9M), record semi-annual margin 26.5% - 24.3% excluding the one-off ~14M US tariff refund, already fully on guidance without it. FY26 guidance reaffirmed for the third consecutive time (revenue mid-to-high SD, margin toward the top of the 25-26% band).

== THESIS READ ==
- The margin machine keeps compounding without capital: no dilution, no buybacks (float ~28.4% already thin - CFO explicit), ~70% payout with explicit special-dividend optionality. Watch: special-dividend decision as net cash builds toward ~1bn.
- iVario penetration and North-America expansion carry the volume story. Watch: US market share vs tariff-era pricing.
- The tariff refund is excluded from the underlying reading (documented) - underlying margin 24.3% is the honest run-rate. Watch: H2 margin ex-one-offs.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
Family-controlled (~55.2% Meister/Wurbser heirs + Kurtz block); 11.4M shares constant across the whole horizon by design. Net cash growing 544 -> 970M with a modest placement yield in the bridge. First population of dernierCall/guidanceHistory/quarterlyEPS/ownership/compliance/coherenceQualitative happened at this cycle's earlier refresh - schema now complete.

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
2026: revenue 1,350M (+7%), EBIT 349M (25.9%), EPS 23.86; 2027-2030: revenue +8.5%/yr, margin ~26-26.7%, conversion ~78% (ETR 24%), shares constant. Watch: Germany/Europe institutional demand; input costs; China localization progress.

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 (Nov); special-dividend announcement window (Mar 2027); iVario milestones; US pricing normalization.

ancrages.moteur: Official FY2026 guidance now reaffirmed three times (Q1 call, IR Talk H1, official H1 release of 06/08): mid-to-high single-digit revenue growth and an EBIT margin targeted towards the high end of the 25-26% range, confirmed by the actual H1 figures (revenue +8% organic, H1 margin 24,3% excluding the tariff effect).

Refund of unduly levied US customs tariffs confirmed in actual figures at ~14 M€, booked as extraordinary operating income in Q2 2026, largely offsetting the Section 232 tariff cost expected for the year (~28-29 M€) - net effect already materialised in the observed H1 26 EBIT margin (26,5% reported, 24,3% excluding the effect), no longer an estimate to be confirmed but now an actual figure.

Structural seasonality of the group (Q1 always the weakest quarter, Q4 the strongest, ~28-29% EBIT margin in Q4 in previous years) confirmed by the sequence Q1 23,9% -> Q2 29,0% (boosted by the tariff refund): H2 operating leverage remains expected, supported by an order book up by 10-15 M€ at the end of June.

Potential market very lightly penetrated (75% of the iCombi market and 96% of the iVario market not addressed) and an installed base of more than 800 000 units generating recurring replacement demand: supports mid-to-high single-digit revenue growth beyond 2026 without depending on a single product driver. Unchanged since creation.

Launch of the iCombi One in China (a local product at a more accessible price, dedicated sales team in place, first key account contract already secured this quarter) and geographic roll-out of the iHexagon: upside still not quantified by management, treated as positive optionality not embedded in the core revenue projection.

Stable distribution policy (payout ratio ~70%, buybacks explicitly ruled out by the CFO given the already low free float) combined with growing free cash-flow generation: the net cash position continues to grow mechanically over the projection horizon.

New anchor (Q2 26): the tariff refund will not recur in 2027 (average tariff expected at ~14% against the earlier assumption of 10%); management is studying several scenarios including a modest price increase if operational efficiency is not enough to absorb the rise in input costs - no precise figure disclosed, treated prudently as a risk/an optionality on the 2027 margin rather than embedded in the core projection.
